cyber.title: Iran-linked intrusions into US water controllers
cyber.summary: A joint FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA and DOE advisory says Iranian-affiliated actors exploited exposed controllers across US critical infrastructure. A late-July FBI warning described pressure loss and flooding in some cases. No supply collapse has been reported.
cyber.us_why: US agencies say US water and energy controllers were accessed. They urge operators to take controllers off the open internet.
cyber.what_to_watch: New advisories reporting service outages at US utilities.

sources.text: Silobreaker says US agencies warned in April that Iran-affiliated actors accessed controllers in water, energy and municipal systems. A late-July FBI warning described pressure loss and flooding in some cases; no supply collapse reported.

The FBI's 2026 alerts page lists a joint FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA, DOE advisory on Iranian-affiliated actors exploiting internet-connected Rockwell/Allen-Bradley controllers across US critical infrastructure. Same equipment is used in the US.
Konbriefing's tracker lists 2026 attacks on US water utilities: Minnesota towns in July, New Jersey in August with a suspected Iran link, and a Michigan well. Service continued in each case.
WaterISAC's bulletin lists a members-only situation report, updated Nov. 12, on heightened risk of Iranian cyber retaliation following US strikes on Iran. Contents are not public.
CSIS says Iran-linked hackers hit US water systems in at least 12 states in August; CyberAv3ngers claimed it, the US has not formally attributed it, and disruption was limited.
NewsNation reports DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullins says Iran has been attempting cyberattacks on the US since February.
Targeted devices included Schneider Electric and Siemens controllers also used in US utilities; CISA and FBI advise taking them off the internet and enabling multifactor authentication.

A secondary summary says FBI-linked warnings cite water utilities in at least seven states reporting incidents since July 27, involving Rockwell MicroLogix controllers; I could not check the primary advisory.

cyber.what_to_watch: A CISA or FBI advisory on Silent Train, or a takedown.

sources.text: BleepingComputer says Silent Train sessions are short, with tools wiped afterward, which makes detection hard. Lumen says it was partly a response to the FBI's earlier KV-botnet takedown.

ai_risk.summary: The main development today is that Trump and Xi agreed that major military decisions made with AI must stay under human control. Separately, Amazon reports that China-linked attackers used AI agents that found and exploited an unknown software flaw on their own. Compared with yesterday, the European Commission breach and central-bank warnings about AI-boosted cyber risk are still developing, UN talks on autonomous weapons moved forward, and METR reports fast growth in AI research skills.

items.title: Amazon: China-linked hackers' AI agents found and used an unknown flaw on their own
items.what: Amazon says China-linked attackers used an AI tool called Cairn whose agents found and exploited a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label software to take over a university server, as reported by The Record and The Register.
items.why: Attackers whose AI finds and uses new flaws without human help could move faster than defenders can patch. If the same approach is turned on power, water or hospital systems, it could cause harm at a much larger scale.
items.who: Amazon security researchers, reported by The Record, The Register and others
items.us: The attacking tool is reported as China-linked, and the same software runs at US research institutions and hospitals.
items.watch: Whether the same AI-agent method appears in attacks on critical infrastructure.

actions.summary: The clearest signals point to fighting continuing for weeks around the Gulf and Red Sea and through the winter in Ukraine. They also point to importing states refilling and pooling oil stocks against prolonged Hormuz disruption; support for these readings is moderate. In Europe, household-kit and reserve steps mostly follow multi-year programmes. No new government steps on NATO's eastern flank appeared in the stories after the reported missile landing in Poland on 20 Nov, so readings there rest on earlier, largely scheduled actions.

patterns.title: Russia and Ukraine keep refilling ranks and planning finances as bridge strikes and…
patterns.points_to: Both sides are keeping the means to fight through the winter while US-mediated talks continue. Ukraine is adjusting deferment rules in both directions: narrowing them for students and reportedly adding a carer deferment. It is also lining up a war-risk insurance fund to start in January.
patterns.unsaid: Setting up a war-risk insurance fund for January suggests Kyiv expects shipping and investment to face war risk into 2027, whatever the talks produce. Russian regions are recruiting reservists while calling mobilisation rumours fake. That is consistent with avoiding a visible call-up while still building up reserves.
patterns.plain_explanation: War-risk insurance is also needed to draw investment after a ceasefire. Deferment changes are routine fine-tuning of a mobilisation system in place since 2022. Russian regional reserve units are part of a programme announced long before.
confirm: Ukraine adopting a lower draft age or ending student deferments
Russia announcing a federal reservist call-up beyond regional units
The insurance fund launching with terms tied to continuing hostilities

recent.text: Large Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy grid continue through the planned Abu Dhabi round.
recent.why: Russia-Ukraine-US talks opened in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, per Anadolu. Large Russian strikes continued: France 24 reported blackouts, three damaged Kyiv bridges and at least seven deaths in the capital around 20-21 November.

recent.text: Limited US-Iran exchanges around Qeshm and Hormuz continue while Qatar-mediated talks go on.
recent.why: Al Jazeera reported tit-for-tat US-Iran strikes and an Iranian claim of a downed US drone over Hormuz on 21 November. Iran also claimed a drone downing near Qeshm.

recent.text: Houthi missile or drone fire toward Saudi cities continues over the next two weeks.
recent.why: Al Jazeera reports the Saudi-led coalition intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh. It was the third night in a row with alerts in the capital. France 24 and AFP also reported Houthi strikes on Riyadh.

recent.text: Military air strikes in Rakhine continue as the army's offensive to retake the state goes on.
recent.why: The Irrawaddy reported that regime air strikes killed over a dozen civilians in Rakhine in the past week. It said the Arakan Army is pushing toward Sittwe and Kyaukphyu. The Diplomat and others also describe an ongoing air campaign there.

recent.text: The Nov 19 Shenzhen meeting takes place without a signed agreement on Iran or Hormuz.
recent.why: The Shenzhen meeting among Trump, Xi and Putin took place on Nov 19. Iranwire reports the joint declaration made no mention of Iran or the Strait of Hormuz, and other outlets report no agreement on Iran came out of it.

recent.text: Fighting and cross-border strikes continuing along the Lahj front toward Aden
recent.why: Reuters, Al Jazeera and AP all report Houthi advances and Saudi-backed reinforcements on the Lahj front, with Tur al-Baha about 80 km from Aden.

recent.text: A deal that reopens Hormuz within two weeks looks unlikely: Iran attaches conditions, and Trump is still floating strikes on nuclear sites.
recent.why: CBS News live coverage on Nov 18 reports no US-Iran agreement. Iran's offer to reopen the strait within two days still depends on its seven conditions, and mediation by Qatar continues.

recent.text: The Abu Dhabi round on Nov 10-11 ending without a ceasefire deal
recent.why: Euronews reports the two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended with no breakthrough on a ceasefire or on territory. The only agreement was in principle, on a prisoner exchange. AP, carried by PBS, also reports no major breakthrough.

recent.text: The Abu Dhabi round on Nov 10-11 is likely to take place, because the Kremlin and the US envoy both confirm it, though no comprehensive deal is on the table.
recent.why: Euronews and AP (via PBS) report that the Abu Dhabi talks took place over two days and ended with a prisoner-exchange agreement but no comprehensive deal.

recent.text: The Abu Dhabi round going ahead on Nov 10-11 is likely; both sides have confirmed delegations or contacts with the US envoys.
recent.why: Euronews reports that Russia and Ukraine held two days of talks in Abu Dhabi with US mediators. AP, via PBS, describes it as the first meeting in nine months.

recent.text: The Abu Dhabi round is likely to go ahead on Nov 10-11, since both Moscow and Washington have confirmed delegations; past rounds produced prisoner swaps but no deal.
recent.why: The round went ahead, and Euronews reports it produced an agreement in principle on a prisoner exchange but no ceasefire or territorial deal. That matches the call as written.

recent.text: The Abu Dhabi round is likely to go ahead with modest results, given both delegations are named and Moscow says it offers no new concessions.
recent.why: The round took place and, per AP (via PBS), ended with a large prisoner exchange confirmed by both sides but no major breakthrough. The Moscow Times says neither side has shown major compromise.
